content.value_statement: Spatial datasets are hard to combine, project, and inspect without domain guidance. This skill guides GeoPandas workflows for vector data, spatial joins, geometry operations, CRS management, and maps.
actual_capabilities: Read and write Shapefile, GeoJSON, GeoPackage, Parquet, Feather, and PostGIS vector data.
Guide CRS checks, CRS assignment, reprojection, and projected CRS choices for measurements.
Explain geometric operations such as buffer, simplify, centroid, convex hull, and affine transforms.
Support spatial joins, nearest joins, overlays, clipping, dissolves, and aggregation workflows.
Create static choropleth maps and interactive maps with GeoPandas plotting integrations.
Suggest performance steps such as bounding box reads, Arrow I/O, spatial indexes, and simplification.
limitations: It covers vector data, not raster imagery or gridded scientific datasets.
It provides guidance and examples, but it does not include executable automation scripts.
Accurate distance and area results still require the user to choose a suitable projected CRS.
Interactive maps, basemaps, and database workflows may require optional Python packages.

use_cases.title: Map zoning and service areas
use_cases.description: Join parcel, boundary, and facility layers to measure coverage and create planning maps.

use_cases.title: Compare habitat and boundary layers
use_cases.description: Overlay protected areas, habitat polygons, and study regions to calculate intersection areas.

use_cases.title: Add spatial context to tabular analysis
use_cases.description: Convert location datasets into GeoDataFrames, match them to polygons, and summarize results by area.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a spatial file
prompt_templates.prompt: Read a GeoJSON file, show its CRS, list geometry types, and summarize the main attribute columns.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare accurate measurements
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether my polygon layer uses a projected CRS, reproject it if needed, and calculate area values in square meters.

prompt_templates.title: Join points to regions
prompt_templates.prompt: Use GeoPandas to join incident points to district polygons, count incidents per district, and explain which predicate to use.

prompt_templates.title: Design a multi-layer map workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a GeoPandas workflow that clips roads to a study area, buffers major roads, joins nearby buildings, and produces a choropleth map.

output_examples.input: Inspect a city parks GeoJSON file before analysis.
output: Loaded the parks layer and confirmed it uses WGS84 coordinates.
Identified polygon and multipolygon features with name, area, and district fields.
Recommended reprojection before any distance or area calculations.

output_examples.input: Find schools within 500 meters of major roads.
output: Recommended projecting both layers to a local meter-based CRS.
Outlined a buffer workflow for major roads and a spatial join for school points.
Suggested validating geometries before the buffer and join steps.

output_examples.input: Create a county-level population density map.
output: Defined a workflow to read county polygons and population attributes.
Recommended calculating density after confirming projected area units.
Outlined a choropleth map with a legend and clear classification choices.

best_practices: Check CRS before spatial operations and use projected CRS values for distance and area measurements.
Filter large files during reads with bounding boxes, masks, rows, or columns when possible.
Validate geometries before overlays, joins, and buffers, then repair invalid features when needed.
anti_patterns: Do not calculate area or distance directly in a geographic CRS such as EPSG:4326.
Do not join layers with mismatched or missing CRS metadata without resolving the CRS first.
Do not rely on Shapefile for complex production data when GeoPackage or Parquet is suitable.

faq.question: What spatial formats does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Shapefile, GeoJSON, GeoPackage, Parquet, Feather, PostGIS, and common cloud or URL-backed vector sources.

faq.question: Can it help with coordinate reference systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains CRS inspection, CRS assignment, reprojection, and choosing projected systems for measurement workflows.

faq.question: Does it support raster analysis?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on vector features such as points, lines, and polygons. Raster workflows need tools such as rasterio.

faq.question: Can it create maps?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers static plots, choropleth maps, layered maps, and interactive map workflows through GeoPandas integrations.

faq.question: How does it handle large datasets?
faq.answer: It recommends filtering during reads, using spatial indexes, simplifying geometries, and using Arrow-backed I/O when appropriate.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill contains documentation and examples. Users decide whether to install packages or run example workflows.
